evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The manager_restarted check requires positive and differing manager PIDs and invocation IDs, but never requires the before/after manager snapshots to share a boot ID. A guest reboot between those snapshots can change both values, causing a reboot to be accepted as an isolated manager restart. The reboot checks already use snapshot boot_id fields, so requiring nonempty equal boot IDs for the manager pair is a routine correctness fix to existing intended behavior, not a new requirement.
